name: Ajvar toast with fried eggs and arugula
intro: Sourdough fried crisp in olive oil, spread thick with smoky ajvar, topped with two runny eggs and a pile of lemony arugula. The jar does the work.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet. Lay the bread in, press it down, and toast until golden and crisp on both sides.
Crack the eggs into the same pan and cook until the whites set and the yolks are still runny.
Spread the ajvar thick on the hot toast.
Toss the arugula with lemon, olive oil, and a pinch of salt.
Egg on each toast, arugula over it, flaky salt.

how_it_works: A great jar turns two eggs into dinner. Ajvar is smoky and sweet, the runny yolk turns it into a sauce, and lemony arugula keeps it from feeling heavy. Any thick, flavorful spread works the same way — this is a template for every month's jar.
swaps: Flaked leftover fish on top instead of the eggs.
Leftover roasted kabocha, crisped in the same pan, under the eggs.
leftovers: Toast doesn't keep. Make it fresh.

make_it_a_meal: Fry a third egg, and spread a spoonful of 2% Greek yogurt under the ajvar — cool and tangy against the smoke.

nutrition.serving: The whole recipe: two eggs on two thick slices of sourdough.
